message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. The first day proved to be a whirlwind of new sights and sounds that left Pebble Spring breathless with wonder. They wandered through narrow alleys where merchants called out the names of their wares in melodic tunes. The smell of freshly baked bread drifted from a dozen small bakeries clustered around the central square. Pebble Spring pressed their mossy hands against the warm stone walls and felt the pulse of life within them. A kind old woman named Marta noticed the curious little figure and offered them a seat by her door. She showed them how the roof tiles were layered to shed rain and how the foundation needed to be deep enough to hold through winter. Pebble Spring listened intently, their leafy ears twitching with every new detail she shared. Over the following weeks, they helped Marta lay the first courses of a small garden shed behind her cottage. The arcane magic in their staff made the stones settle into place with an almost musical hum. Neighbors began to gather, curious about the strange Leshy who spoke to the rocks as if they were old friends. Children would press their faces close to the walls, watching the magic ripple through the mortar like ripples in a stream. Pebble Spring found themselves growing a little taller each week, their root-feet sinking deeper into the packed earth. The city was not just a collection of buildings, they realized, but a living thing with its own rhythm and breath. Every house held a secret, every corner hid a story that had been whispered and rewhispered for generations. They learned that a wall was more than stone; it was a promise between the builder and the sky. The bridges, too, taught them lessons about balance and the courage of reaching across divides. As autumn crept in, the leaves on Pebble Spring's head turned golden and then a deep russet red. They could feel the city settling into its long sleep, the hearth-fires flickering to life in every window. With a contented sigh that rustled like dry leaves on a path, they settled their staff against the newest wall they had built. Pebble Spring would often sit upon the weathered and mossy stones of the ancient wooden bridge, carefully watching the merchants and farmers carrying their heavy wares through the bustling marketplace while noticing how the spotty pattern of sunlight fell across the cobblestones below.
